newsitem.title: CANADA: NOVA files load-retention toll deal.
newsitem.headline: NOVA files load-retention toll deal.

text.p: NOVA Corp pipeline unit NOVA Gas Transmission Ltd said on Friday it filed its application with Alberta's energy regulator for approval of a toll deal struck to avert a competing pipeline project.

The load-retention toll agreement would provide shippers that signed precedent agreements with PanCanadian Petroleum Ltd's Palliser Pipeline with a short-haul, restricted service with comparatively fewer options and a longer average contract term, NGTL said.

The deal, announced late last year, effectively killed PanCanadian's plans for the competing Alberta pipeline but also signalled the end of the "postage stamp" tolling system, in which all shippers paid the same to move gas on NGTL regardless of distance.

"NGT's application acknowledges that a single postage-stamp rate no longer is sufficiently flexible to meet the increasingly diverging interests of our customers, including distance of haul," Bob Schmidt, NGTL's vice-president of regulatory affairs, said in a statement.
"It is just the kind of industry-driven, competitive solution that Alberta's Minister of Energy was calling for."
The proposed load-retention service rate is 15.5 cents (Canadian) per thousand cubic feet effective January 1998, and will escalate by two percent per year up to 20 years.
Alberta Energy and Utilities Board approval of the deal would raise the existing postage-stamp rate to all other shippers by less than one cent per MCF, NGTL said.
